exposure: Maternal Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection status (HCV RNA positive vs. negative, and HCV antibody positive vs. negative)
cohort: The study participants included pregnant women categorized into three groups based on their Hepatitis C virus (HCV) antibody and RNA status.
finding: Chronic HCV infection affects the liver function of pregnant women and HCV RNA positivity is an independent risk factor for neonatal jaundice, but it does not increase pregnancy or delivery complication risks or neonatal malformation rates.
